note: Round 2, against corpus-osv-ecosystems-v2: all 251,912 OSV records flattened to one .txt per advisory (same per-source licences as the mirror NOTICE: GHSA CC-BY-4.0, OpenSSF MAL Apache-2.0, EEF CC-BY-4.0, Drupal MIT, GSD CC0). Round-1 mirror shape (raw per-ecosystem JSONs) was never indexed: the ghsa-db round-1 diagnosis (issue #1158) showed raw JSON maps to typed records with no `text` field, invisible to `xerj code` passage search — caught before this build burned. Queries and expect clauses byte-identical to the round-1 suite (pre-registered blind 2026-10-04); expect_file re-pinned to the flattened records, whitespace-normalised grep-verified. Pre-registered before any round-2 retrieval.

queries.q: We depend on org.apache.sshd:sshd-common 2.9.3; which Apache MINA SSHD release addressed the Terrapin attack, and is patching the server side alone enough?
queries.expect: The mitigations to prevent this type of attack were implemented in Apache MINA SSHD 2.12.0, both client and server side

queries.q: With Composer 2.2.23 fetching packages as git clones instead of dist archives, which composer subcommands can an attacker abuse through a poisoned branch name to run code?
queries.expect: The `status`, `reinstall` and `remove` commands with packages installed from source via git containing specially crafted branch names

queries.q: How does the Devise confirmable email-change race condition let an attacker wind up with somebody else's address confirmed on their own account?
queries.expect: The confirmation token is sent to an email the attacker controls, but the `unconfirmed_email` in the database points to a victim's email address

queries.q: On a dual-stack Node deployment, why can one abusive IPv4 visitor push every other IPv4 user of express-rate-limit into 429 responses?
queries.expect: This collapses all IPv4 traffic into a single rate-limit bucket: one client exhausting the limit causes HTTP 429 for all other IPv4 clients

queries.q: Why can a session token stolen earlier still authenticate after the user signs out of an ash_authentication_phoenix app?
queries.expect: a token obtained before sign-out, through script injection, interception or device theft, keeps authenticating until its own expiry
